open_points.subject: self-service password reset request
open_points.text: Status says “a token is issued and delivered only for an existing verified address,” while R0-23 and A10 say the password-reset request “does nothing” and creates, audits, or delivers nothing.
open_points.question: In the accepted State 2 behavior, does a password-reset request for an existing verified account issue and deliver a token, or remain inert?
options: Issue and deliver a PasswordResetToken for an existing verified account.
Return the concealed normal response but create and deliver nothing.
open_points.default_guess: Keep the running-service behavior: return the concealed response and do nothing.

witness.initial: An active staff account has a verified email and no outstanding reset token.
events: An unauthenticated person submits that email to the password-reset request operation.
outcomes: A PasswordResetToken and delivery are created for the account.
No token, delivery, audit record, or other state change is created.
witness.observer: The account holder, the email gateway, and an operator inspecting persisted records.

open_points.subject: trusted-host, CORS-allowlist, and public-origin runtime settings
open_points.text: A25 says “Trusted hosts, the CORS allowlist and the public origin are three separate runtime settings (A30),” but A30 does not give these settings’ environment-variable names, types, requiredness, defaults, normalization, or complete validation rules.
open_points.question: What is the exact runtime configuration contract for each of the three transport settings, especially whether public origin is required and what happens when it is absent or malformed?
options: Require trusted hosts and public origin at startup, allow an empty CORS allowlist, and reject malformed values.
Require trusted hosts, but permit public origin to be absent and consequently refuse every viewer sign-out.
Provide explicit defaults for one or more of the settings.
open_points.default_guess: Require a nonempty trusted-host list and one canonical public origin at startup; default the CORS allowlist to empty; reject malformed values.

witness.initial: A deployment supplies trusted hosts but supplies no public-origin setting.
events: A viewer with an active cookie sends sign-out with an Origin header matching the site being used.
outcomes: Startup is refused because the canonical public origin is required.
Startup succeeds, but sign-out is refused because no configured public origin can match.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and the viewer.

open_points.subject: deployment binding of runtime knobs
open_points.text: The changed heading says “Runtime knobs with confirmed defaults (deployment values may differ),” while R0-10 says configuration comes only from environment variables, but most listed knobs have no environment-variable name and no other deployment binding.
open_points.question: Which environment variable, if any, overrides each timeout, TTL, rate limit, and entropy knob, and are omitted variables replaced by the listed defaults?
options: Define a fixed environment-variable name for every deployable knob and use the listed value when omitted.
Only the rows naming an `_env_name` are environment-backed; all other listed values remain source-fixed.
Use a different explicit deployment mapping.
open_points.default_guess: Define fixed uppercase environment-variable names for every deployable knob and apply the listed values as defaults when they are absent.

witness.initial: A deployment needs staff sessions to last 6 hours instead of the confirmed 12-hour default.
events: The operator sets an intuitively named environment variable such as STAFF_SESSION_TTL_HOURS=6.
The service starts and later issues a staff session.
outcomes: The service recognizes that variable and issues a 6-hour session.
The service ignores that name and issues a 12-hour session because another name, or no override, was implemented.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and the staff member whose session expiry differs.

open_points.subject: validation of configurable numeric values
open_points.text: A30 says deployment values may differ and that “an invalid or missing required variable stops start-up,” but it defines positivity only for BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES and gives no accepted ranges or zero-value semantics for timeouts, TTLs, the challenge rate limit, or credential entropy.
open_points.question: For every configurable numeric knob, which values are valid, and must zero, negative, fractional, excessively large, or otherwise malformed values stop startup?
options: Require positive integers for TTLs, rate limits, and entropy and a positive finite number for timeouts.
Permit zero for selected knobs as a way to disable or immediately expire the associated behavior.
Define individual bounds and disablement semantics per knob.
open_points.default_guess: Reject zero and negative values; require integral TTL, rate-limit, and entropy values and positive finite timeouts.

events: A staff member successfully logs in.
outcomes: Startup is refused because a zero TTL is invalid.
Startup succeeds and creates a session that is expired immediately.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and the logging-in staff member.
